title: Zero-Dependency Portfolio Architecture
summary: A data-driven, multi-page web platform engineered with semantic HTML5, modular CSS token systems, and vanilla ES5/ES6 JavaScript—delivering sub-second loads with zero client framework overhead.
description: Designed and built from scratch to prove that expressive interfaces do not require megabytes of client-side JavaScript bundles. Every page hydrates from structured JSON schemas through a custom declarative data-binding kernel (`data-bind`, `data-list`, and shared HTML partials) while maintaining complete accessibility and progressive enhancement.
highlights: Declarative DOM hydration engine (`content.js` + `data-loader.js`) binding nested JSON paths and `<template>` lists without virtual-DOM overhead
Synchronized dual-palette token architecture (`variables.css`) with instant pre-paint theme resolution and zero flash of unstyled content
Dual-runtime deployment pipeline supporting Express development serving and hardened Nginx production containers with SHA-versioned assets
imageAlt: Architectural diagram and dark-mode UI specimen of the zero-dependency portfolio system

documentation.heading: Architectural Overview
documentation.body:
Modern web portfolios frequently over-engineer simple document delivery with heavy single-page application frameworks. This project takes the opposite stance: treat the browser's native platform as the framework.

Shared chrome (`navbar.html`, `footer.html`, `background.html`) is injected asynchronously by `app-loader.js`, while page copy and collections are stored in structured JSON files under `data/`. This separation allows copy, projects, and timeline milestones to evolve without touching layout markup.

documentation.heading: Declarative Data-Binding Kernel
documentation.body:
The `content.js` module traverses the DOM for `data-bind`, `data-bind-html`, `data-bind-src`, and `data-list` attributes, resolving dot-delimited paths against `pages.json`:

- **Text & Attribute Binding**: Safely assigns `textContent` and attributes (`src`, `alt`, `href`) without XSS surface area.
- **Template Cloning**: Clones native `<template>` fragments for action buttons, timeline milestones, and skill matrices.
- **Graceful Degradation**: Every HTML file includes meaningful default copy in its static markup so the page remains readable even before scripts finish executing.

documentation.heading: Production Hardening & CI Pipeline
documentation.body: In production, `scripts/version-assets.sh` computes an 8-character SHA-256 digest for every CSS and JS file, rewrites all HTML references, and packages the output into an Alpine Nginx image with strict `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, and `nosniff` headers.

title: Mathematical Orb Timeline & Motion Engine
summary: A scroll-pinned horizontal experience timeline powered by pure-function slope geometry, CSS custom properties, and full screen-reader and keyboard navigation parity.
description: An interactive career and learning journey visualization that maps chronological milestones onto a rising geometric trail. A standalone math kernel calculates normalized ascent ratios and Euclidean connector vectors (`--rise`, `--slope-angle`, `--slope-length`), while a scroll-driven runway pins the viewport on desktop and falls back to native snap scrolling on touch devices.
highlights: Pure-function geometry kernel (`timeline-math.js`) decoupled from the DOM so date parsing, rise normalization, and trigonometry run in Node unit tests
Zero-jitter height reservation pass (`is-measuring`) that measures all expanded detail rows in a single frame before painting
Full keyboard (`ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `Home`, `End`), dot-button, and `aria-live="polite"` screen-reader announcement support
imageAlt: Visualization of the mathematical orb timeline showing glowing cobalt nodes and diagonal slope vectors

documentation.heading: Separating Pure Math from DOM Rendering
documentation.body:
To guarantee deterministic layout across screen sizes, the timeline splits into two files:

1. **`timeline-math.js`**: Pure functions (`parseDate`, `computeRises`, `computeSlopes`, `formatAnnouncement`) with zero DOM references, exported to both `window.TimelineMath` and CommonJS `module.exports`.
2. **`timeline.js`**: Reads the computed values and applies them as CSS custom properties (`--rise`, `--slope-angle`, `--slope-length`) on each `.timeline-entry`.

documentation.heading: Single-Frame Height Reservation
documentation.body: Collapsing and expanding detail cards inside a horizontal track normally causes the section height to jump as the user scrolls. The renderer solves this by applying `.is-measuring` (which forces `grid-template-rows: 1fr` with `transition: none`), reading the tallest detail block via `getBoundingClientRect().height`, storing `--timeline-detail-height` on the track, and removing `.is-measuring` within the same paint frame.

documentation.heading: Scroll-Pinned Runway & Reduced Motion
documentation.body: On fine-pointer desktop viewports (`min-width: 960px` and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`), `.timeline-pin` becomes `position: sticky` inside a calculated vertical runway so vertical wheel scrolling smoothly advances the horizontal track. On touch screens or when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active, the runway collapses and native horizontal scroll-snapping takes over automatically.

title: Client-Side MVC Contact & Opportunity Engine
summary: A pure-model contact and opportunity scoping system with real-time validation, deep-linked brief hydration, clipboard synthesis, and RFC-compliant mailto dispatch.
description: Built to eliminate conversion friction between reviewing a developer portfolio and initiating a concrete technical conversation. Combines an interactive Opportunity & Capability Matcher on the homepage with a full MVC contact workspace that validates payloads, formats structured briefs, and supports instant clipboard or email client handoff without requiring a backend database.
highlights: Strict separation between pure validation/formatting logic (`contact-model.js` & `opportunity-studio.js`) and DOM event wiring (`contact-form.js`)
Interactive Opportunity & Scope Studio that maps role/project intent and technical stack priorities to verified codebase proof points
Seamless URL state handoff (`?topic=...&subject=...&message=...`) from homepage brief composer directly into the full contact workspace
imageAlt: UI system diagram of the client-side MVC contact workspace and interactive opportunity studio

documentation.heading: Why Client-Side MVC for Static & Hybrid Hosting
documentation.body:
Static and container-hosted portfolios often fail at the final conversion step: either they rely on third-party form endpoints that break or rate-limit, or they drop a raw `mailto:` link with zero context.

By structuring the contact flow as a client-side MVC system (`contact-model.js` + `opportunity-studio.js` + `contact-form.js`), visitors get guided topic presets, character-counted validation, formatted plain-text brief synthesis, and one-click clipboard or email dispatch.

documentation.heading: Interactive Opportunity Studio Integration
documentation.body: The Opportunity Studio lets recruiters and collaborators select their intent (`Frontend / Full-Stack Role`, `Project Collaboration`, or `Architecture Walkthrough`) and toggle specific engineering capabilities. It immediately surfaces matching proof points from the portfolio and generates a tailored inquiry brief that can be sent immediately or opened in `contact.html` via URL query hydration.
